studies.Population: European American and African American adults aged 20-79 years with renal cell carcinoma or controls
studies.Smoking Status: Never, occasional/unknown, former, or current; adjusted for smoking history
studies.Ethnicity Basis: Population imputation: stated Black/African population -> Black
studies.Ethnicity Supporting Text: 1142 EA and AA RCC cases and 1154 frequency-matched controls
studies.Reference: Renal cell carcinoma risk associated with lower intake of micronutrients.
studies.Authors: Bock CH, Ruterbusch JJ, Holowatyj AN, Steck SE, Van Dyke AL, Ho WJ, Cote ML, Hofmann JN, Davis F, Graubard BI, Schwartz KL, Purdue MP
studies.Timing: Usual adult diet prior to two years ago
studies.comparison_type: Lowest quartile (<=144 mg/day) versus highest quartile (>666 mg/day)
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Dietary micronutrient intake was derived from an interviewer-administered diet history questionnaire.

sample_size.excerpt: 1142 EA and AA RCC cases and 1154 frequency-matched controls were enrolled in a population-based case-control study between 2002 and 2007.
sample_size.location: Methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 1142 + 1154 = 2296

cases.excerpt: 1142 EA and AA RCC cases and 1154 frequency-matched controls were enrolled in a population-based case-control study between 2002 and 2007.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Associations between individual micronutrients and RCC risk were assessed using unconditional logistic regression models to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) from adjusted models. These analyses were weighted using a jackknife replication method (Jackknife 2).
